$comment: Cross-workspace import ratchet baseline — enforced by app/scripts/lint-workspace-imports.mjs,
wired into each EPR app's `pnpm run lint`.
Every directory in app/ that ships to users is an EPR app: an independently built,
content-addressed bundle. That is a DEPLOYMENT boundary. It is not automatically a module
boundary, because each app's tsconfig `paths` maps sibling `@app/<pillar>/*` aliases directly
at the other workspace's private `src/app/*` tree — deep paths, both directions, no public API.
The edges below are therefore DECLARED DEBT, not an approved architecture. The rail fails on a
new specifier or a higher count; shrinking is the only allowed direction. When a direction
reaches zero, delete its entry — the seam is then real and cannot silently reopen.
Standing debt this baseline freezes (arch-frontend-bundle-seams-backlog.md, rows 1-2):
* The graph is CYCLIC. elohim-app -> lamad and lamad -> elohim-app both carry live edges.
* The arrow runs core -> pillar. `@app/lamad/models/content-node.model` is the single
heaviest edge in the repo: the cross-pillar content substrate lives inside the learning
bundle, and the `elohim` pillar (which root CLAUDE.md names the owner of cross-pillar
services) imports it. Placement decision is open and is an architect call.
* lamad's tsconfig comment attributes its reverse edges to a controlled composition root.
That is not what the tree shows: models/, services/, interfaces/, utils/, guards/ and
quiz-engine/ all reach back. Trust this file's counts, not that comment.

elohim-app.note: Shell -> lamad bundle. Dominated by models/content-node.model (the cross-pillar content substrate) — see rows 1-2. Ratchet down only.

lamad.note: lamad bundle -> shell pillars. Claimed to be composition-root-only; is not. Ratchet down only.
